summary: Okta SSO sessions invalidated for multi-region users after DST/timezone claim mismatch
description:
Issue summary: Several internal users in eu-west and us-east started reporting immediate SSO logouts and 401s when attempting to access internal consoles (Grafana, Model Observability, and internal billing dashboards) between 2026-03-13 07:00-10:30 UTC.

Impact: Intermittent but widespread login failures for multi-region staff and automation jobs using short-lived service sessions. Affects interactive console sessions and some CI systems that exchange Okta session tokens. No customer-facing services impacted.

Observed behavior: Users report they are redirected to Okta auth, authorise successfully, and then immediately get logged out with a 401. SRE traces show session cookie present but token validation fails due to claim mismatch between 'iat'/'exp' and our sessionFingerprint rotation check.

Expected behavior: Okta SSO tokens should be accepted if signature and expiry are valid; session fingerprint rotation and claim checks should be tolerant to timezone/DST differences across datacenter/time-source boundaries.

Initial detection: Pager alert from identity-proxy that token validation failure rate spiked at 2026-03-13T07:05:00Z. Slack thread: #oncall -> https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C12345/p1776.

Steps to reproduce: See 'steps_to_reproduce' field for a short reproducer that mimics the failing validation path.
steps_to_reproduce: Use dev Okta test user in eu-west region and perform SSO flow to console (OIDC code flow)
Observe token exchange in identity-proxy logs -> token signed by Okta, with iat/exp in ISO8601 UTC
Force system clock on a proxy node to UTC+1 while Okta-issued token retains UTC timestamp (simulating DST transition)
Retry token exchange and observe identity-proxy rejecting token with mismatch error and immediate 401 returned to client
investigation_notes:
Summary of findings (first 24h):
- Identity-proxy validation component compares token 'iat'/'exp' claims and also calculates a sessionFingerprint TTL using local epoch seconds. After the recent DST push and an NTP slip on a subset of eu-west proxies, local epoch drifted by ~3600s on ~18% of proxy nodes.
- Okta tokens are valid (verified signature and exp > now on authoritative NTP nodes), but proxy nodes with drift see 'iat' > now (token not yet valid) or 'exp' < now (already expired) and reject.
- Logs sample: "token_validation_error: claim_iat_in_future delta_seconds=3598 node=ip-10-5-3-77.eu-west identity_proxy_v2"
- Affected components: identity-proxy (primary), session-rotation job (secondary).
- Related runbook: CONFLUENCE-IDS/Runbooks/okta-token-validation (link in related_confluence_pages).

Hypothesis: A combination of NTP drift on a subset of identity-proxy nodes and a recent tightening of token clock skew tolerance in our validation library (PR: github.com/redwood/identity-proxy/pulls/402) caused otherwise-valid Okta-issued tokens to be rejected during DST boundary activity across regions.
comments: Avery Chen (2026-03-13 08:10): Initial triage - rolling restart of eu-west identity-proxy pool to get fresh NTP sync. Cannot replicate on staging.
Samir Patel (2026-03-13 08:22): Confirmed NTP on ip-10-5-3-77 was 3599s ahead. Restarted ntpclient and identity-proxy on that node; token validation errors stopped for users routed to that node.
Infrastructure (2026-03-13 09:01): Scheduling rolling NTP sync and diagnostic across all identity-proxy autoscaling groups; potential kernel time_sync settings being ignored on some AMIs.
Maya Gonzalez (security) (2026-03-13 10:05): Noted recent validation library change - acceptable clock_skew reduced from 300s to 60s in PR 402. Is that intended?
Samir Patel (2026-03-13 11:00): Temporarily reverted clock_skew tolerance to 300s via config flag in identity-proxy to restore availability while infra completes NTP remediation.
Avery Chen (2026-03-14 02:12): Running post-mitigation validation across eu-west and us-east; error rate has fallen to baseline. Continuing to monitor for 72h.
workaround: Deployed temporary config change to identity-proxy to increase accepted clock_skew to 300 seconds and performed rolling restart of proxy nodes in eu-west. This restored access for affected users. We should treat this as mitigation only - underlying NTP drift must be fixed.
next_steps: Complete infra NTP remediation across all identity-proxy ASGs and verify kernel time_sync settings (owner: infra)
Harden AMI boot scripts to include ntp/chrony health checks (owner: infra)
Revert temporary clock_skew tolerance change after infra fixes and release a measured library update that is resilient to short clock drifts (owner: identity-proxy team)
Add synthetic check to our SRE dashboards that simulates Okta token validation to catch clock skew regressions early (owner: SRE)
Post-incident blameless write-up and runbook update (owner: oncall)
